Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
During `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, only the top-level/global scope of the PKGBUILD is sourced. The code at that level performs standard variable and array definitions, appends to the `pkgname` and `source` arrays, and uses `eval` to dynamically generate package functions from the hardcoded `_languages` array. No `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions execute at this stage. The `eval` calls construct function definitions from locally defined, hardcoded locale strings — a common AUR pattern for generating i18n subpackages — and do not evaluate external or untrusted input. The `source` array entries point to the official Mozilla archive. No network requests, downloads, or arbitrary command execution occur during sourcing. The hardcoded `_google_api_key` is a string assignment that is inert during `--printsrcinfo` (it is only written to a file inside `prepare()`, which does not run here).
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Top-level code in the PKGBUILD is standard packaging logic; no malicious execution during --printsrcinfo.</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- Top-level code in the PKGBUILD is standard packaging logic; no malicious execution during --printsrcinfo.

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD builds Firefox ESR from Mozilla's archive and installs locale XPI packages also from Mozilla's archive. The only dynamic shell construct is `eval "package_$_pkgname() { _package_i18n $_lang }"`; it generates package function names from a static local language list and does not execute downloaded content or arbitrary attacker-controlled input.

No evidence of exfiltration, reverse shells, hidden decoding, or execution of fetched code. Packaging operations are limited to applying local patches, configuring the Mozilla build, installing files under `$pkgdir`, and installing locale XPIs as Firefox extensions. Checksums/PGP metadata are present for the upstream source; the `SKIP` entry corresponds to the detached signature source and is not, by itself, malicious.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Standard Firefox packaging with no malicious behavior</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This .SRCINFO file is a standard Arch Linux package metadata file for Firefox ESR with internationalization (i18n) language packs. It declares package information, dependencies, and sources all from the official Mozilla archive (archive.mozilla.org). The PGP key (14F26682D0916CDD81E37B6D61B7B526D98F0353) is Mozilla's official release signing key. All sources are fetched from Mozilla's official release infrastructure, checksums are provided for all files (with one SKIP for the .asc signature file, which is standard practice), and there is no executable code, network commands, obfuscation, or any behavior beyond standard package building. This represents normal, legitimate AUR packaging.
</details>
